newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nampo says 1.3 mln T S.Africa maize set for export.
newsitem.headline: Nampo says 1.3 mln T S.Africa maize set for export.

text.p: South Africa's National Maize Producers Organisation (Nampo) said on Wednesday that 1.3 million tonnes of the country's 1997 maize crop had already been committed for export.
"It has been confirmed to us by shippers and export agents that 1.3 million tonnes of white and yellow maize has been contracted for exports," Japie Grobler, Nampo's chairman told Reuters.
Grobler said that if the high level of exports was subtracted from the country's 1997 crop estimate and carryover stock from last year, there would be a shortage of white maize this year.

"Even if the crop estimate is 10 to 15 percent higher on white, we will still be in a shortage position...This means that the price for white maize will have to rise sharply to match demand for available stocks," he said.
Latest official crop estimate figures peg South Africa's maize harvest at 7.660 million tonnes, which is between one or two million tonnes above consumption.
The crop is expected to comprise 4.139 million tonnes of white maize and 3.521 million tonnes of yellow. The next estimate is due on July 21.
Grobler said there was about 600,000 tonnes of white carryover stock.
He said the yellow maize position was still uncertain in view of yield and quality problems in the eastern Mpumulanga province and eastern Free State region.
